target: the stem is leafless apart from reduced leaves: cauline leaf PO_0000013 + lower FLOPO_0991377 + scale-like FLOPO_0991143 (lanceolate); no normal stem leaves

target: leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106 absent PATO_0000462; oral setae (trichome PO_0000282 at the sheath mouth) absent PATO_0000462
fix: In bamboos and grasses, 'auricles' means leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106 and 'oral setae' means trichomes at the sheath mouth (PO_0000282). Never map either to stipule. 'X and Y absent' gives an absence for each noun. 'Culm sheath' is a sheath on the culm (leaf sheath PO_0020104 or scale leaf), not a stipule.

target: no annotation: 'flowers not known' means the data is missing, not that the plant lacks flowers
fix: '<part> not known / not seen / unknown / not yet collected' records that the part was not observed. Emit no annotation, and never emit absent PATO_0000462.
reason: The fruiting cymes show the plant does flower. The flowers were simply not collected.

target: absence of the leafy bracts around the head cluster (bract PO_0009055 subtending the capitula, absent PATO_0000462); the scarious tips belong to the phyllaries (involucral bract PO_0009045)
fix: In Asteraceae, 'ebracteate' (capitula or head cluster ebracteate) means no leafy bracts outside the involucre. The phyllaries (involucral bract PO_0009045) are not affected. Never map phyllary qualities such as 'tips scarious' to generic bract.
reason: In Leontopodium, the 'star' of leafy bracts around the heads is a diagnostic character, and some species lack it. The phyllaries, with their scarious tips, are always there.

target: no annotation: 'flowers not seen' means missing data
fix: '<part> not seen / not known / unknown' records that the part was not observed. Emit no annotation, and never emit absent PATO_0000462.

target: leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106 absent PATO_0000462 (oral setae absent too); remove the 'present' record
fix: A phrase that ends in 'absent' / 'lacking' / 'wanting' must never give 'present'. In 'X and Y absent', the absence applies to every noun in the list.

target: leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106 absent PATO_0000462 (probably on the foliage-leaf sheaths); 'stiffly pale yellow hairy' describes the culm sheath (leaf sheath PO_0020104 hairy PATO_0000454), not a stipule
fix: In Poaceae and bamboos, 'auricles' means leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106. Never map it to stipule PO_0020041. A hairiness clause in a culm-sheath sentence belongs to the sheath.

target: 'unequal' belongs to the umbel rays (the stalks of the partial umbels; peduncle PO_0009053, unequal length) or to the bracteoles PO_0009043, not to the absent involucral bracts
fix: In Apiaceae, 'bracts' are the involucre of the compound umbel and 'bracteoles' are the involucel. A bare quality after 'bracts absent; rays N' belongs to the rays (or the next named part), never to the bracts just said to be absent.
reason: The typical Apiaceae sentence is 'Umbels ...; bracts absent; rays 8-15, unequal'. The quality was carried back onto the bracts.

target: no bracts outside the involucre (calyculus or peduncle bracts: bract PO_0009055 on peduncle PO_0009053, absent PATO_0000462); the phyllaries (involucral bract PO_0009045) are white-ciliate
fix: In Asteraceae, 'capitula not bracteate / ebracteate / without calyculus' means no bracts outside the phyllaries. Never read it as 'bract absent' for the taxon when involucral bracts are described.

target: leaves present only at the stem apex: cauline leaf PO_0000013 + upper FLOPO_0991376 present; the stem below is leafless
fix: 'leafless except at/near the apex/base' and 'leafy only above' place the leaves in that region (leaf + upper FLOPO_0991376 or basal FLOPO_0991002). Never read them as leaf absent.
reason: The 'except' clause states that leaves exist. The ovate-oblong leaves are the apical ones.

target: cauline leaf PO_0000013 decreased amount PATO_0001997 (stem with few leaves)
fix: 'almost / nearly / ± / subleafless' and 'almost absent' are hedged statements. Read them as decreased amount PATO_0001997 of the part (or skip them), never as absent PATO_0000462.
reason: 'Almost leafless' means the stem has a few leaves. Basal leaves are also described.

target: vascular leaf PO_0009025 + basal FLOPO_0991002 absent PATO_0000462; the cauline leaves (PO_0000013) are ± orbicular
fix: 'Basal leaves absent' / 'radical leaves absent' / 'rosette absent': keep the position (basal FLOPO_0991002 or rosette leaf PO_0000014) as part of the absence. Never fall back to 'leaf absent'.
reason: Only the basal leaves are missing. The orbicular leaves are the stem leaves.

target: style PO_0009074 absent PATO_0000462 in ray flowers (PO_0025331; sterile rays); the disc-flower style or its branches are linear
fix: In Asteraceae, an absence of style, ovary or pappus in a ray-floret clause belongs to the ray flower PO_0025331. Disc-floret parts described in the same taxon are not contradicted. Keep the floret type as context.
reason: Bidens has sterile ray florets without a style, while the disc florets have styles with linear branches.

target: 'pubescente sur la face externe' describes the fig receptacle (syconium; inflorescence PO_0009049 or fruit PO_0009001) outer surface pubescent PATO_0000455, not a bract
fix: In Ficus, 'réceptacle/figue ... sans bractées externes, pubescente sur la face externe': the surface quality agrees with the receptacle (the feminine 'figue') and belongs to it. Do not attach it to the bracts just said to be absent.
reason: The absence (no external bracts on the fig) is correct. The pubescence is that of the fig wall.

target: ostiole without externally visible (outer) ostiolar bracts (bract PO_0009055 + outer FLOPO_0991379 at the ostiole, absent PATO_0000462); the basal bracts of the fig (bract + basal FLOPO_0991002) are puberulous
fix: In Ficus, keep the bract position (ostiolar, lateral, basal) with any absence. 'ostiole sans bractées externes' and 'without lateral bracts' do not deny the basal bracts.

target: lateral bracts on the fig wall (bract PO_0009055 + lateral PATO_0001193) absent PATO_0000462; the apical (ostiolar) bracts are present and short
fix: In Ficus, 'without lateral bracts' means bracts on the receptacle wall are absent. Keep the position in the absence, and never read it as 'bract absent'.
reason: The apical ostiolar bracts and the lateral wall bracts are different sets.

target: cystoliths in the leaf lamina absent: idioblast PO_0000283 (cystolith-bearing cell; no PO class for cystolith) part of leaf lamina PO_0020039, absent PATO_0000462
fix: 'cystoliths absent / without cystoliths' and other cell or inclusion nouns (raphides, crystals, dots) are the bearer of the absence. Never fall back to the organ being described.

target: leaf lamina PO_0020039 not punctate (no dots; negation of PATO_0001512 punctate)
fix: 'dots absent / without dots / not dotted / epunctate' means the lamina surface has no dots. Annotate the lamina as not punctate (PATO_0001512) and never as leaf absent.
reason: In Myristicaceae, the minute dark dots on the lamina are a key character. Their absence says nothing about the leaf.

target: leaf lamina PO_0020039 not punctate (no dots; negation of PATO_0001512 punctate)

target: glume PO_0009039 without awn (awn PO_0025349 absent on the glumes); the lemma PO_0009037 is short-awned

target: lower glume PO_0006002 absent PATO_0000462; the upper glume is pubescent

target: petal PO_0009032 absent PATO_0000462 in pistillate flowers (PO_0025599); the staminate-flower petals are tiny

target: leaf PO_0025034 (leaf blade or sheath) scaly PATO_0001804 (lepidote); the stem is absent

target: no annotation for the fruit ('capsules not seen' means missing data); 'throat circular' belongs to the perianth tube throat (perianth PO_0009058), not the fruit

target: palea PO_0009038 absent PATO_0000462 in the sterile (basal barren) florets; the fertile floret's palea is 1-keeled

target: 'muticous' belongs to another part (the glumes, glume PO_0009039, or the sterile-floret lemmas): awn absent there; the fertile lemma PO_0009037 is awned
fix: In Poaceae, 'muticous' / 'awnless' qualifies the part named in its clause (glumes, sterile lemmas). Attach the awn absence to that part, never to the taxon.

target: trichome PO_0000282 absent on the leaf (leaf PO_0025034 glabrous PATO_0000453)

target: annulus (thickened ring at the mouth of the perianth tube; perianth PO_0009058, no PO class for annulus) absent PATO_0000462; 'pilose' also belongs to the perianth, not the corolla

target: caudex (woody perennial stem base; listed only as a synonym of stem PO_0009047, no PO class of its own) absent PATO_0000462; the flowering stems are present. 'not fistulose' means the stem is not hollow (solid), not 'stem hollow'
